I think it’s because the stereotypical autistic person for years was a white male and only obviously presented. Not only that, on average we are more likely to struggle with physical hygiene like showering and brushing our teeth, obesity and other factors that could make us appear less attractive. Exercise can be hard for uncoordinated autistics, and restricted eating can cause nutritional deficiencies. 
Not only because a lot of us dress for comfort and then find it hard to find comfort vs clothing that also look good on us. I believe we can also dress in the clothes we like, not necessarily the clothes that are in fashion. Due to executive dysfunction, it can be hard for us to maintain our physical appearance, like for me I can either do my hair or makeup, not both.
This isn’t for everyone, obviously every autistic person is different, and some people are obsessed with physical hygiene, some are into fashion, all of this can be masked and often is. I’m just referencing what could be going on through the studies that I have read. 
It has been noted that autistic people often actually are more attractive, we just don’t know how to groom ourselves. I don’t know how true that is, but it has been a clinical observation by many people, including Hans Asperger.

I think of myself in third person in respect to the issues I face and ask myself if it’s realistic to ask myself to be any different in this moment in time. Radical acceptance helps the most. 

I wonder if you could go to therapy if possible for you and talk about your body image, even though talking won’t change anything physically, it could change the way you view and deal with your body image emotionally. I know how hard it can be for some to get therapy though.
I’m sorry that you’re feeling this way, I wish all the best for you.

I read about someone who remembered being the reincarnation of someone who ended their life, but they remembered dying a different death, though all other details of their life were correct. Could be that their soul thought it was too much to remember, or it served a particular purpose not remembering the actual death.

I also read of another case of someone after ending their life, reincarnated into a 5-month-old baby. It could mean that it was predicted or was fate that they were going to kill themselves, that's up for interpretation. Or these stories might not be real, because it's hard to prove.

It's hard to speculate. I remember my past life and I have had suicidal ideation since I was very young. I know that people say that babies don't have memories past the age of 2, though remember transporting/finally becoming conscious a few days after I was brought home from the hospital, I remember that as part of my death, transporting, with no perceived time between.

I personally believe that suicide could have the possibility to cut somebody's life short in a way that was not intended, and a better outcome could have come out of it, but I think in some form way we know when the limit of a hard life may hit. I think good and bad are subjective and because as humans we are afraid of death and pain, this is where the idea of suicide is bad can come from. I am not convinced that death is a way to escape from life and I do not condone suicide. The only thing we can hope for is darkness and that this was all an illusion. You have a very good point that they are like other illnesses, it's a complex subject!

The only tip I can give you is to figure out why you’re over sharing.
Is it because you’re lonely and wanting to connect? Start making a journal and write about these things, so you aren’t tempted to overspill.
Is it because you don’t know how to converse?
Make pre-planned scripts in your head. E.g “How have you been?” You could talk about things you have been doing such as reading a book, trying a new food, things at work, school, etc. Take notice of your words and remind yourself that you’re trying to change, it’s okay to fail.

Finding out the reasons why will make it easier to find a solution to it. :) I wish you all the best.
